nodes.description: Within the eIF4F cap-binding complex, eIF4A resolves secondary structure in the 5' leader so that the 43S preinitiation complex can be loaded and can scan to the start codon; pharmacological clamping of eIF4A1/eIF4A2 onto RNA blocks exactly these steps. eIF4A2 recognises the 5' cap structure, permits mRNA loading onto the ribosome, and binds preferentially in the translation initiation region spanning the 5' UTR and the adjacent start of the coding sequence. Importantly, eIF4A2 loss does not collapse bulk protein synthesis - global translation rates are unchanged in eIF4A2-depleted cells - so the disease-relevant consequence is a shift in which mRNAs are efficiently initiated, not a general translational shutdown.

nodes.description: Because eIF4A2 both activates initiation on some transcripts and represses others via Ccr4-Not, its disruption reshapes a specific translational program rather than reducing protein output globally. In embryonic stem cells, eIF4A2 activates translation of pluripotency-factor and histone H3.3 mRNAs while restricting the totipotent two-cell program, and its knockdown disrupts the proteome and causes loss of cell identity - the clearest experimental demonstration that eIF4A2 dosage sets a developmental cell-fate program through translation. The disease-relevant claim, that the equivalent program in developing human neurons is what fails in NEDHSS, is an extension from stem-cell and invertebrate systems and is therefore provisional.

meta.association: EIF4A2 (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A2, also known as DDX2B) is the single causal gene for NEDHSS. Both extremely rare de novo mono-allelic variants and inherited bi-allelic variants have been reported, across 15 individuals from 14 families, with a further mosaic proband described subsequently. Causality rests on the recurrence of ultra-rare variants across unrelated families, molecular modelling showing perturbation of key protein domains, and in vivo Drosophila rescue assays in which human EIF4A2 wild-type cDNA rescued eIF4A loss-of-function pupal lethality while the variant cDNAs failed or only incompletely rescued it. The evidence supports both loss- and gain-of-function as operating mechanisms across the allelic series, which is why the entry does not model a single directional dosage lesion.

nodes.description: eIF4A2 uses ATP binding and hydrolysis to remodel RNA. The disease variants are predicted to perturb the interfaces that couple ATP hydrolysis to RNA duplex remodelling. Both loss and gain of function are proposed for different alleles: in the Drosophila rescue assay some variant cDNAs behaved as hypomorphs while others produced variant-specific defects not explained by simple loss of activity, and the discovery authors concluded that both mechanisms operate. The helicase activity itself is functionally required - helicase-dead eIF4A2 mutants fail to rescue eIF4A2 depletion in embryonic stem cells - so an activity lesion is mechanistically sufficient to matter.

nodes.description: Separately from its activating role in eIF4F, eIF4A2 is a major effector of the repressive microRNA pathway. It binds the MA3 and MIF4G domains of CNOT1 - competing with DDX6 for the same site - and, once incorporated into Ccr4-Not, represses target mRNAs at the initiation step by binding purine-rich motifs in the 5' UTR immediately upstream of the AUG. Which helicase is recruited also determines the fate of the transcript: eIF4A2 inhibits CNOT7 deadenylase activity whereas DDX6 enhances it, so eIF4A2-bound mRNAs keep longer poly(A) tails. In EIF4A2-variant patient fibroblasts this arm is measurably broken: eIF4A2 and Ccr4-Not show significantly reduced colocalization and the Ccr4-Not target IMP1 is abnormally elevated.

nodes.description: NEDHSS is caused by extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2, which encodes the DEAD-box ATP-dependent RNA helicase eIF4A2 (DDX2B). Molecular modelling of the reported variants predicts that they perturb structural interactions within key domains of the protein. DEAD-box helicases are built from two conserved RecA-like domains that jointly form the RNA- and ATP-binding surface, so substitutions within or between these domains are expected to alter RNA binding, ATP hydrolysis, or the coupling between them.

nodes.description: Truncating EIF4A2 alleles reduce eIF4A2 protein abundance. In fibroblasts from carriers of the heterozygous frameshift deletion c.896_897del, eIF4A2 protein was reduced to approximately half of the normal level, establishing haploinsufficiency as a real, measurable consequence of truncating EIF4A2 alleles. nodes.description: Epilepsy is a defining feature of the cohort, reflected in the OMIM entity name qualifier "with or without seizures". Seizure onset is typically early and the semiology reported in detail so far is epileptic spasms.

evidence.reference_title: Rare EIF4A2 variants are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, hypotonia, and epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2

nodes.description: Mouse embryonic stem cells subjected to shRNA knockdown of eIF4A2, with wild-type and helicase-dead rescue arms, profiled by eCLIP-seq, ribosome profiling, SILAC proteomics and RNA-seq. This is the system that defines what eIF4A2 actually does to a developmental translation program, and it supplies the negative control that eIF4A2 loss does not reduce global translation.

evidence.reference_title: eIF4A2 targets developmental potency and histone H3.3 transcripts for translational control of stem cell pluripotency.
evidence.snippet: As initiation is the rate-limiting step of translation, we carried out an RNA interference screen for key translation initiation factors required to maintain embryonic stem cell (ESC) identity.
